title: L in the Source stops dead at the Out mark; I can't play past it to find a later out
wanted: Shuttle past the current Out in the Source to pick a later out point, as in Premiere
did: Double-clicked shot 3 on the timeline (Source opened with In 0:00 / Out 7:01), pressed L from 5:08, then L again, then K+L, then the Source Play button
happened: L ran to 00:00:07:01 and stopped exactly on the Out mark; a second L, K+L did nothing (stays 7:01). The Play button at the Out jumped back to the In and played from there (read 1:10). The only way past the Out is to drag the Source scrubber. In Premiere marks never stop J K L.
expected: J K L and Play run to the end of the clip regardless of In/Out (Shift+Ctrl+Space plays In to Out)
suggestion: Let L / Play run past the Out; keep 'play In to Out' as its own command

title: Double-click a timeline shot: Source opens at the frame I clicked but the timeline playhead jumps to the shot's first frame, so the two monitors show different frames
wanted: Open the timeline shot in Source at the frame I'm looking at, to re-mark it
did: Playhead parked at 5:21 in shot 1; double-clicked shot 3's body at about 16 s
happened: Source: GX010483 at 00:00:05:08 with In/Out set to the shot (toast says so, good). But the sequence playhead jumped to 00:00:11:02 (shot 3's first frame), so Program shows a different moment than Source. Match frame is lost.
expected: Either both at the clicked frame or Source at the playhead's frame (Premiere's match frame, F)

title: Typed timecode: digits mean different things depending on a sign or a colon (100 = 1 s, -100 = 100 frames, 1:00 = 1 minute)
wanted: Move the playhead by typing, the Premiere way: 100 = 1 second, +100 = forward 1 second, 1:00 = 1 second
did: Ctrl+G (and click on the timeline timecode), typed 5108, +15, 300, 3000, 1:00, -1:00, 10:30, -100
happened: Absolute digits work like Premiere (5108 → 51:08, 300 → 3:00, 3000 → 30:00, +15 → +15 frames). But -100 moved back 100 FRAMES (1:35:10 → 1:31:06), not 1 second; and '1:00' went to 1 MINUTE, '10:30' to 10 min 30 (clamped to the end), '-1:00' to the first frame. The hint says '1:05' is a valid form, but not what it means. My hands typed -1:00 for 'back a second' and landed at 0:00.
expected: One grammar: digits are timecode read from the right (frames last), with or without a sign or colons
suggestion: Read +100 / -100 as ±1 s like Premiere, and colons from the right (SS:FF); show the parsed result in the toast ('1:00 → 00:01:00:00')

title: Ctrl+V inserts and ripples the film; there is no overwrite paste, and Ctrl+Shift+V does nothing, silently
wanted: Paste a copied shot over what's at the playhead (Premiere Ctrl+V = overwrite, Ctrl+Shift+V = insert)
did: Copied shot 2 (3.7 s), parked at 30:00 inside shot 5, Ctrl+V; undid; Ctrl+Shift+V at the same spot
happened: Ctrl+V split shot 5 and pushed everything after it 3.7 s later (1:35:11 → 1:39:04). The toast says exactly that and offers 'at the next cut instead', which is nice. Ctrl+Shift+V: nothing changed and no message. Ctrl+X also closes the hole (ripple) where Premiere's leaves a gap. My Premiere hands will knock the sync of anything on V2 / music out every time I paste.
expected: Ctrl+V overwrites on the targeted track, Ctrl+Shift+V inserts; or at least Ctrl+Shift+V says what it does here
suggestion: Make Ctrl+Shift+V the insert paste and Ctrl+V the overwrite paste, or keep insert but answer Ctrl+Shift+V with a message

title: The Source timecode can't be typed into: Ctrl+G with the Source focused moves the sequence, and typed digits + Enter start 'this shot only' playback in Program
wanted: Jump the Source to 10:00 in GX010493 by typing, to mark a 2 s cutaway
did: Source focused (blue border) with GX010493 loaded: Ctrl+G, 1000 Enter; then clicked the Source timecode 00:00:09:07 and typed 1000 Enter
happened: Ctrl+G opened the timeline's field and moved the SEQUENCE playhead to 10:00; the Source stayed at 9:07. Clicking the Source timecode opens nothing; the digits went nowhere and Enter started the Program playing shot 2 with '· this shot only' on its readout (same trap as last round's HANDS-08, now on the Source side).
expected: Click the Source timecode (or Ctrl+G while the Source has focus) to type a source time
suggestion: Same typed-timecode field on the Source; Ctrl+G acts on the focused monitor

title: Right after laying a V2 cutaway, Program showed the cutaway one frame past its end (at 4:00, where V1 should be)
wanted: Check the out of the cutaway frame-accurately
did: Overwrote a 2:00 cutaway (In 9:07 / Out 11:07, 'In-Out 00:00:02:00') to V2 at 2:00 with '.', playhead landed at 4:00; waited 1.5 s; stepped ← to 3:23 then → to 4:00
happened: Both looks at 4:00 right after the edit showed the ski cutaway; 4:01 showed the bar. Jumping there by timecode later, and three more step tries, showed the bar at 4:00 correctly. So for a moment after the edit the Program drew a stale frame at the cut point. 2 of 5 looks wrong, both in the first ~5 s after the edit.
expected: The frame after the cutaway's last frame is always V1

title: A selected transition looks the same as an unselected one, its shot stays outlined, and Delete on it gives no message
wanted: Select the fade-in at the film's start and delete it, knowing it's the fade (not the shot) that goes
did: Zoomed in (=), clicked the purple fade box on shot 1's head (tooltip says 'Delete removes it'), Delete; then clicked the audio fade and Delete again
happened: After the click the fade box looked exactly as before (side-by-side shots identical) and shot 1 still had its white selection outline, so I had to guess whether Delete would ripple-delete the shot. Delete did remove only the video dissolve (Program at 0:00 no longer black) but nothing was said; the only trace was the undo tooltip 'undo: delete Cross Dissolve'. The audio fade stays separate (fine, Premiere does that too), also deleted silently. Effect Controls kept showing shot 1's Lumetri, not the transition.
expected: Selected transition highlighted, shot de-selected, Effect Controls shows the transition (duration, alignment), toast 'removed Cross Dissolve at 0:00'
suggestion: Draw a bright outline on the selected transition and drop the shot's outline; toast every Delete

title: Typing a transition length: '12' became a 7.34 s dissolve over two whole shots, silently; the field is 15 px wide
wanted: Set the dissolve to 12 frames by typing (Premiere: double-click, type 12 = 12 frames)
did: Double-clicked the 8-frame dissolve between shots 1 and 2, Ctrl+A, typed 12, Enter
happened: The field that opened is about 15 px wide inside the transition box: I could not read what I typed. '12' was taken as 12 SECONDS and clamped to 7.34 s: the dissolve now covered all of shot 2 and half of shot 1, hatched red, with no message about the clamp. Only the tooltip (which I found by reading the field's hover text) says 'seconds (or frames: 12f)'. Undo put it back; '12f' gave 0.50 s correctly.
expected: A readable duration field (or dialog) that reads digits as timecode like everywhere else (12 = 12 frames, 100 = 1 s), and says when it clamps
suggestion: Open a proper small popover with the current length in timecode; refuse or warn on anything longer than the media allows

title: Moving the playhead (typed timecode, ↑/↓, Home) moves the selection to the shot under it, so Delete removed a shot I never clicked
wanted: Delete the shot I last clicked (shot 1), after jumping the playhead to check something at 1:00:00
did: Clicked shot 1 (chip: 'Shot 1 · GX010474'), Ctrl+G 10000 Enter, Delete
happened: The jump silently moved the selection to shot 9 (chip changed to 'Shot 9 · GX010489', white outline moved); Delete then removed shot 9, my 23.9 s half-speed run, and rippled the film 1:47:09 → 1:23:13. The toast named it and Ctrl+Z brought it back, but in Premiere moving the playhead never changes what is selected, so my hands deleted the wrong shot. Also: a single click on a shot moves the playhead to that shot's first frame.
expected: Selection changes only when I click or use a select key; Delete acts on that; with nothing selected Delete does nothing
suggestion: Decouple 'the shot at the playhead' (for the AI scope and Effect Controls) from the selection Delete acts on, or at least don't draw it as a selection

title: The Playback Resolution dropdown slides along the Program's bottom row as the readout text changes
wanted: Find the resolution dropdown in the same place every time
did: Looked at the Program bottom row on first load, with a shot selected, and while 'this shot only' playback ran
happened: Its centre was at x=1803 on first load, 1702 with the '00:01:47:09 3/13 · GX010483' readout, and about 1611 with '· this shot only' added. The transport buttons themselves stayed put in every state (Play/Pause 1439, prev/next 1388/1490, Source 393–556), which is the part that matters.
suggestion: Pin the dropdown to the right edge and let the readout take the space to its left

title: The Source monitor has an Insert button but no Overwrite button
wanted: Overwrite from the Source with a click, as with Premiere's two buttons under the Source
did: Looked along the Source transport row and its tooltips
happened: Mark In, Mark Out, step, Play, step, 'Insert (,)'. Overwrite exists only as the '.' key (the V1/V2 tooltip says so). Fine for my hands, but the mouse path is half there.

title: The cut menu still shows two running times for one cut (1:47 and 1:35) after a speed change
wanted: Read my cut's length in the cut switcher
did: Opened the cut switcher after setting shot 9 to ½×
happened: 'The cut 13 shots · 1:47' at the top, 'main 13 shots · 1:35' in the CUTS list, 1:47:09 on the timeline. Same as round 1's HANDS-19.

title: I can't park past the end: a typed time beyond the film lands on the LAST frame, so an overwrite 'past the end' ate the last frame of my shot
wanted: Overwrite a 2 s source range after the end of a 2 s sequence (Premiere: park after the end, '.' appends or leaves a gap)
did: On a copy with one 2:00 shot, Ctrl+G 1000 Enter (10 s), then '.'
happened: The playhead went to 00:00:01:23, the last frame (End goes to 2:00, the end point, but a typed time doesn't), with no 'past the end' message. '.' then overwrote from 1:23: the first shot lost its final frame (source out 11.30 → 11.26) and the film is 3:23, not 4:00. The toast said 'overwrote … at 00:00:01:23', which is how I noticed. Earlier '+2:00:00' and '10:30' on the main cut also landed on the last frame (1:35:10) rather than the end (1:35:11).
expected: A time past the end parks at the end point (after the last frame), like End does, so an overwrite appends
where: Typed timecode clamp / Overwrite at the end
suggestion: Clamp to the duration, not duration minus one frame

title: Select all (Ctrl+A) + Delete left the V2 cutaway behind while the screen says the sequence is empty
wanted: Empty a copy of the cut to test editing into an empty sequence
did: Ctrl+A on the timeline, Delete
happened: Toast: 'removed 13 shots (1 … 13 · 107.5 s)'. V1 and A1 emptied, but my 2 s V2 cutaway stayed at 2:00, floating over nothing, while Program said 'the sequence is empty' and Effect Controls 'Nothing selected — the sequence is empty'. After I inserted a 2 s shot, the cutaway sat past the film's end (film 2:00, cutaway 2:00–4:00).

title: Rotate clip is outside Ctrl+Z, and it is the only thing on a Project clip's right-click menu
wanted: Undo a clip rotation I picked by mistake the way I undo everything else; right-click a clip for the usual clip actions
did: Right-click GX010475 in Project › Rotate clip › 90° right; then looked at the ↶ tooltip
happened: The ↶ tooltip still said 'undo: overwrite' (my previous edit), so Ctrl+Z would have undone an edit, not the rotation; the only way back is the toast's own Undo (gone after a few seconds) or right-click › 'As decided (automatic)'. The right-click menu has nothing but Rotate clip: no Open in Source, Insert, Overwrite, Reveal, Rename. The timeline thumbnails of a rotated shot also stay unrotated.

title: Sequence Settings has no frame size, shape or frame rate, and with a shot selected the menu item does nothing visible
wanted: Make a 9:16 copy of my film: set the copy's frame shape, then reframe each shot
did: On a copy: Sequence › Sequence Settings… with a shot selected (twice), then with nothing selected
happened: With a shot selected, nothing visible happened (Effect Controls kept the shot). With nothing selected, Effect Controls shows 'Sequence copper-02-2026 · 2 shots · 0:03 · look none · auto-balance on · 2 warnings', no resolution, aspect or fps anywhere. Position / Scale / Rotation + 'Fill the frame' exist per shot, but with no 9:16 frame there is nothing to reframe into. (The builders said vertical is not built; confirming it is not there.)
suggestion: Either a real settings dialog (frame size, fps) or rename the item to what it shows

title: Undo history of my main cut was gone after I saved a copy, worked on it and switched back
wanted: Come back to main and still Ctrl+Z my last edits there
did: On main (↶ said 'undo: Cross Dissolve duration'), Save copy as 'scratch-empty' with 'work on the copy' ticked, edited the copy, then switched back to main in the cut menu ('on main' toast)
happened: On main both ↶ and ↷ were greyed: 'nothing to undo', 'nothing to redo'; Ctrl+Z did nothing. Main's content was intact (13 shots, 1:47:09, my ½× and V2 cutaway still there). Round 1's complaint was losing undo on reload; now it's lost on a cut switch.
expected: Each cut keeps its own undo history across switches (the builders say it survives a project switch)

title: What Shift+Delete removes depends on invisible state: once the shot at the playhead, once a transition I'd added two steps earlier
wanted: Ripple-delete the shot at the playhead after jumping there (the selection-follows-playhead rule I had just learned)
did: Shift+D added an audio fade at a cut; then Ctrl+G 3000 Enter (inside another shot), Shift+Delete
happened: It deleted the audio fade I'd added (undo tooltip 'delete Constant Power'), not the shot under the playhead, whereas earlier a typed jump moved the selection to the shot under the playhead and Delete removed that shot (R2-09). With an edit point selected after '}', Shift+Delete at 60:00 did nothing. Three different targets for the same key in ten minutes; the only clue is which thing has the faint outline.
expected: One rule: Delete acts on what I clicked last, and the screen highlights it clearly

title: After a fit (\), the timeline re-fits itself on every length change, so shots slide out from under my next click
wanted: Razor a shot twice and click the middle piece to ripple-delete it
did: Pressed \ to fit, set shot 9's speed ½× → 1× (film 1:47 → 1:35), worked out the middle piece's x from the ruler I'd just looked at, clicked it, Shift+Delete
happened: The ruler had re-scaled (fit to the new length: 15 s marks moved from 111 px apart to 125 px), so my click landed on the cut before shot 9 and selected an edit point; Shift+Delete said 'nothing to delete at this edit'. Round 1 I saw the same rescale after ripple deletes and pastes. In Premiere \ fits once; the zoom then stays until I change it.
suggestion: Keep the zoom level the editor set; only re-fit when they press \

title: Bracket trims move 6 frames (¼ s), and 'Shift: a second' for the in-point can't be typed: Shift+] is } and trims the OUT
wanted: Trim shot 4's head by a second from the keyboard, as the key sheet says ('[ ] trim the in-point (Shift: a second)')
did: Selected shot 4, pressed Shift+] twice; then measured ], [, }, { once each against the server
happened: Shift+] extended the shot's OUT by 1 s each time (film 1:23:20 → 1:25:20) because on my keyboard Shift+] is '}', the out-point key. Plain ] / [ / } / { each move their point by 0.25 s = 6 frames, not a frame. So the sheet's in-point-by-a-second is unreachable, and the bracket keys are too coarse for a frame trim (Alt+←/→ on a selected edit is the frame trim).
expected: [ ] a frame, Shift a bigger step, on keys that can actually be pressed
suggestion: Use Alt/Ctrl with [ ] for the bigger step, or say '¼ s' on the sheet

title: Right-click on a timeline shot offers only 'Ask AI about this…' and 'Look deeper…'
wanted: Right-click a shot for the clip actions my hands reach for (Speed/Duration, Paste Attributes, Ripple Delete, Unlink, Enable, Reveal in Project)
did: Right-clicked GX010488 on V1
happened: Two items, both AI. Every manual action lives in a key, a menu bar item, or Effect Controls. Clip menu: Mark In/Out (Source), Insert, Transcript…, 'Speed and colour… → Effect Controls'. For a hands-first editor the right-click is the AI's, not mine.

title: My first edit to the title's words was thrown away when I went on to the y field
wanted: Change the title's words by hand, then its height and timing
did: Clicked in 'words', Ctrl+A, typed 'COPPER · FEB 2026', then double-clicked the y field and typed 74 Enter, then in 0.5 and 'for' 3.5
happened: y, in and for took; the words box went back to 'COPPER MOUNTAIN · FEB 2026' (the card re-rendered while it was 'checking…'). Second try (type, then Tab) stuck. A person who doesn't look back at the box would accept the old words.
